ITQAN:v3p292/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p292/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p292/r6.claim: Some classify al-Shu'ara as istitrād because the discourse returns afterward to prophets and earlier communities.
ITQAN:v3p292/r6.anchor: وفي الشعراء إلى ذكر الأنبياء والأمم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.claim: Exegetes cite various proofs that all of Abraham's requests were granted except his prayer concerning his father.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.anchor: Müfessirler, İbrâhim’in babasının affı dışındaki bütün dileklerinin kabul olunduğuna dair çeşitli deliller getirmişlerdir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.claim: The exception about the sound-hearted is God’s own completion and explanation of Abraham’s prayer; if a child could benefit his parent, Azar would have benefited from having Abraham as a son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.anchor: These words are not part of Abraham’s prayer. They are in fact from God Himself and complete and explain the prayer.

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r1.claim: The verse means that no one's wealth will help on Resurrection Day, even if spent on good works, and no one's sons will help, even if righteous and capable of intercession.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r1.anchor: بدل من يوم يبعثون ومفعول الفعل محذوف والتقدير لا ينفع مال أحدا وإن كان مصروفا في الدنيا إلى وجوه البر والخيرات ولا ينفع بنون فردا

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.speaker: ليث
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.claim: Al-Layth says disbelievers boasted of wealth and children, but these cannot help without sound hearts; Muslims benefit from good deeds and from righteous children, whether the child dies first or later prays for the parent.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.anchor: قال الليث : كان الكفار يقولون : نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r3.speaker: بحر
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r3.claim: Baḥr reads the day when wealth and children do not help as the approach to the divine presence for acceptance of God's grace.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r3.anchor: وفي "البحر" : {يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون} للوصول إلى الحضرة لقبول الفيض الإلهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r6.claim: يوم لا ينفع is an appositive to يوم يبعثون; wealth and sons cannot ransom or defend their owners as they can in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r6.anchor: وأتى فيهم: يوم لا ينفع بدل من: يوم يبعثون. مال ولا بنون: أي كما ينفع في الدنيا يفديه ماله ويذب عنه بنوه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r7.claim: Some interpret البنين broadly as all helpers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that attachment to worldly life and its attractions will not help; wealth and children are named as its most prominent adornments.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r8.anchor: وقيل: المعنى يوم لا ينفع إعلاق بالدنيا ومحاسنها، فقصد من ذلك الذكر العظيم والأكثر، لأن المال والبنين هي زينة الحياة الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r12.claim: The account of the Resurrection uses past-tense verbs in أتى, أزلفت, and برزت to present the events as certain after the rebuke of the idolaters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r12.anchor: ولما وبخهم وقرعهم، أخبر عن حال يوم القيامة، وجيء في ذلك كله بلفظ الماضي في أتى وأزلفت وبرزت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.claim: The apparent reading makes all these clauses part of Abraham's speech, reporting what God taught him about his people and the Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الجمل كلها متعلقة بقول إبراهيم، أخبر بما أعلمه الله من أحوال يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya separates “the day when wealth and children do not benefit” from Abraham's speech, treating it as God's description of the Day Abraham feared being disgraced on.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وهذه الآيات من قوله: يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون هي عندي منقطعة من كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that separation: if the phrase is an apposition to the day of resurrection, its governing verb cannot make it God's separate speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r5.anchor: وعلى كلا التقديرين، لا يصح أن يكون من كلام الله، إذ يصير التقدير: ولا تخزني يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r1.claim: This phrase is apposition to the Day of Resurrection, heightening that day's terror and preparing for the following exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r1.anchor: بدل من ( يوم يبعثون ) جيء به تأكيدا لتهويل ذلك اليوم وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من الاستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r2.claim: Abraham continues speaking through the statement that there is a sign in this.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r2.anchor: وهو إلى قوله تعالى ( إن في ذلك لآية ) الخ من كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya instead treats these verses as a separate divine report describing the day Abraham asked God not to disgrace him; the author says apposition rules this out.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r3.anchor: وابن عطية بعد أن أعرب الظرف بدلا من الظرف الأول قال : إن هذه الآيات عندي منقطعة عن كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r4.claim: بنون means sons in its ordinary sense; another view understands it as all helpers.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r4.anchor: والمراد بالنون معناه المتبادر وقيل : المراد بهم جميع الاعوان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r5.claim: The phrase can mean that none of the world's goods and adornments benefits; wealth and sons are singled out as its chief adornments.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : المعنى يوم لاينفع شيء من محاسن الدنيا وزينتها واقتصر على ذكر المال والبنين لأنهما معظم المحاسن والزينة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r1.claim: On that day wealth cannot ransom someone or be given to an intercessor or powerful defender, and sons cannot support or console; other things are even less useful.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r1.anchor: يفتدي به أو يبذله لشافع أو ناصر مقاهر

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r1.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r1.claim: Ali says wealth and children are the world's harvest, while good deeds are the afterlife's harvest; God may grant both to some people.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r1.anchor: عن أبي حمزة الثمالي حدثني غير واحد ، عن يحيى بن عقيل قال : قال علي _ رضي الله عنه _ : المال والبنون حرث الدنيا والعمل الصالح حرث الاخرة

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r2.speaker: الثرى
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r2.claim: Al-Thari explains that wealth is called māl because it inclines people toward itself.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783/r2.anchor: قال : سمعت الثرى قال : انما سمي المال لانه يميل بالناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.claim: “Yawm” is appositional to the earlier “day they are raised,” linking this scene to resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r1.anchor: يوم بدل من الأولى في قوله يوم يبعثون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.claim: The verse negates worldly attachments and names wealth and children as the greatest adornments of worldly life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r2.anchor: فقصد من ذلك العظم والأكثر لأن المال والبنين هي زينة الحياة الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r5.claim: Wealth cannot protect anyone from God's punishment, even if offered as much gold as the earth holds or all its people as ransom; children likewise cannot help.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r5.anchor: لا يقي المرء (4) من عذاب الله ماله، ولو افتدى بملء الأرض ذهبا: {ولا بنون} ولو افتدى بمن في الأرض جميعا

MUQATIL:26:86-89/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:86-89/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:86-89/r3.claim: After death, neither wealth nor children protect anyone from punishment.
MUQATIL:26:86-89/r3.anchor: { يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون } [آية: 88] من العذاب من بعد الموت،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#9/r1.claim: This day is an appositive to the earlier mention of day.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#9/r2.claim: On that day neither wealth nor children benefit anyone.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r11.claim: The Day phrase is an apposition to the earlier day; sons means supporters, since if one's son cannot help, no one else will.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r11.anchor: { يوم } بدل من { يوم } الأول. أي يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون أحدا. والمراد بقوله: { ولا بنون } الأعوان

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r12.claim: Another explanation says sons are singled out because Abraham's father has just been mentioned: Abraham could not benefit him.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r12.anchor: وقيل: ذكر البنين لأنه جرى ذكر والد إبراهيم، أي لم ينفعه إبراهيم.

STUDYQURAN:26:88/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:88/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:88/r1.claim: Wealth and children, sources of worldly status, security, and comfort, are useless in the Hereafter; this is a recurring Quranic theme.
STUDYQURAN:26:88/r1.anchor: The uselessness in the Hereafter of wealth and children, which exalt human beings and are a source of security, status, and comfort in this world

SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r1.claim: Yawma lā yanfaʿ is an appositional substitute for the preceding day, 26:87.
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r1.anchor: قوله: { يوم لا ينفع }: بدل من " يوم " قبله.

SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah makes God's speech continue through the following verses and parses this day as a substitute for the day they are raised.
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r2.anchor: وجعل ابن عطية هذا من كلام الله تعالى إلى آخر الآيات مع إعرابه " يوم لا ينفع " بدلا من " يوم يبعثون ".

SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r3.claim: The author rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyyah's parsing: the substitute shares its governor with its antecedent, which cannot work across the change of speaker.
SAMIN-DURR:26:88/r3.anchor: ورده الشيخ: بأن العامل في البدل هو العامل في المبدل منه، أو آخر مثله مقدر.

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r1.claim: Abraham's plea not to be disgraced shows that people need God's support at Resurrection: the weak human constitution cannot face its terrors without divine aid.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r1.anchor: ويعلم من سؤاله عدم الإخزاء يوم القيامة أن الإنسان في حاجة إلى النصر الإلهي

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r2.claim: The phrase about the Day wealth and children do not avail is appositional to the Day people are raised, so Abraham's speech continues; this refutes the claim that his speech ends at the earlier phrase and the following fifteen verses are God's words.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r2.anchor: الظرف بدل من قوله { يوم يبعثون } وبه يندفع قول من قال إن قول إبراهيم قد انقطع

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r3.claim: Money and children fail because their worldly function as social bonds of mutual support is only conventional; Resurrection discloses reality and severs such ties.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r3.anchor: رابطة المال والبنين التي هي المناط في التناصر والتعاضد في الدنيا هي رابطة وهمية اجتماعية

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r4.claim: The denial concerns the socially assigned causal power of wealth and children, which serve worldly aims, and by extension signifies the failure of all conventionally valued means to material benefits, such as learning, craft, and beauty.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r4.anchor: فالمال والبنون عمدة ما يركن إليهما ويتعلق بهما الإنسان في الحياة الدنيا فنفي نفعهما يوم القيامة كالكناية عن نفي نفع كل سبب وضعي اعتباري

TABRISI:26:72-77/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r5.claim: In “except the one who comes to God,” the noun and relative clause may be accusative as a substitute for the omitted object of “benefit”: no person, wealth, or children benefit except that person.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r5.anchor: إلا من أتى الله الموصول والصلة في محل النصب على البدل من مفعول ينفع المحذوف تقديره يوم لا ينفع أحدا مال ولا بنون

TABRISI:26:72-77/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r6.claim: Alternatively, the relative clause is accusative as an exception.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r6.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن يكون منصوبا على الاستثناء

TABRISI:26:85-89/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:85-89/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:85-89/r5.claim: On that Day, wealth cannot ransom its owner from hardship, and children cannot bear any of their parent's sins.
TABRISI:26:85-89/r5.anchor: إذ لا يتهيأ لذي المال أن يفتدي من شدائد ذلك اليوم به ولا يحتمل من صاحب البنين بنوه شيئا من معاصيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75/r1.claim: The object of “benefit” is omitted because it is understood: wealth and children will benefit no one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75/r1.anchor: ومفعول النفع محذوف للعلم به كأنه قيل: لا ينفع مال ولا بنون أحدا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.claim: Qatāda, as transmitted by Saʿīd, says the sound heart is free of associationism.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: أي: من الشرك، في تفسير سعيد، عن قتادة.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.claim: Vocative truncation can drop jointly added final letters: عثمان becomes عثم, مروان مرو, and أسماء أسم; poets provide matching examples.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.anchor: وذلك قولك في عثمان يا عثم أقبل وفي مروان يا مرو أقبل

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.claim: Paired suffixes are removed together when they were added together, as with مسلمان; a name like بنون loses only نون, since names cannot be shorter than three letters, and the remainder may be treated as an unaugmented name.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكفيعثمانياعثمأقبلوفيمروا.anchor: وكذلك ترخيم رجل يقال له مسلمون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1032/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1032/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1032/r1.claim: بنون is an appendage to the sound masculine plural; when that plural is in an iḍāfa construction, its nūn is dropped, giving forms such as بنو آدم and بني آدم.

NASHR:v1p455/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r1.claim: In spellings such as mayah, mayatayn, malayh, and malayhim, the alif before yāʾ is additional and the yāʾ represents the hamza.
NASHR:v1p455/r1.anchor: فالألف في ذلك زائدة كما قدمنا

NASHR:v1p455/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jazari rejects al-Dani, al-Shatibi, and their followers' claim that the yāʾ in malayh and malayhim is additional: it is the hamza's written form.
NASHR:v1p455/r2.anchor: من الداني والشاطبي ومن قلدهما كيف قطعوا بزيادة الياء

NASHR:v1p455/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r3.claim: Some initial hamzas are written according to how they are eased in connected speech, applying the medial spelling pattern to indicate that easing combines two Arabic pronunciations.
NASHR:v1p455/r3.anchor: بل صورت بحسب ما تخفف به حالة وصلها بما قبلها

NASHR:v1p455/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r4.claim: The dammated hamza in unabbikum is represented by waw after alif; comparable paired hamzas in other words are written with one alif to combine both written forms.
NASHR:v1p455/r4.anchor: فرسمت المضمومة في (أونبيكم) بالواو بعد الألف

NASHR:v1p455/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r5.claim: The same conventions cover paired and triple hamzas and selected initial-hamza forms written with yāʾ to represent connected pronunciation.
NASHR:v1p455/r5.anchor: وكذلك ما اجتمع فيه ثلاث ألفات لفظا نحو أآلهتنا

NASHR:v1p455/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r6.claim: Hāʾulāʾ is written with waw and joined to the alerting particle with its alif omitted, as in yā ayyuhā.
NASHR:v1p455/r6.anchor: ثم وصل بها التنبيه بحذف ألفه كما فعل في (يأيها)

NASHR:v1p455/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r7.claim: In the Taha spelling yābna umm, the waw joins the word and the following alif belongs to ibn, not to the vocative particle, whose alif is omitted.
NASHR:v1p455/r7.anchor: فالألف التي بعد الياء هي ألف (ابن)

NASHR:v1p455/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن السخاوي
NASHR:v1p455/r8.claim: Al-Sakhawi identified the Damascus codex as evidence for the yābna umm spelling, and Ibn al-Jazari says he saw the same reading there, though the manuscript showed a mark of erasure.

NASHR:v1p455/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p455/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p455/r9.claim: The Sham codex cited by al-Sakhawi is kept at the northeastern Mashhad Ali in Damascus's Umayyad Mosque; trusted teachers said it had earlier been in the al-Kushk mosque in Damascus.
NASHR:v1p455/r9.anchor: بالمشهد الشرقي الشمالي الذي يقال له مشهد علي بالجامع الأموي

DURR-FULL:v6p306/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha asked whether Ibn Judʿān’s hospitality and care for kin would benefit him; the Prophet answered no, because he never prayed for forgiveness for his sin on Judgment Day.
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r5.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت: يا رسول الله إن ابن جدعان كان يقري الضيف ويصل الرحم
